dayClock._doc: The day's one clock (ui/game/dayClock.js): the hour shown in the top bar, run by the town and country maps (1 real minute an hour) and moved on by what you do anywhere. Every action point spent passes hoursPerAP hours (travel, work, trading, audiences...), so a full day's maxActionPoints (10) fills the waking day from wakeHour (8 AM) to about 11 PM. Time passed in person (walking a town, work on the map, sleep) costs points in turn: you can never hold more action points than the hours left before midnight allow (floor(hoursLeft / hoursPerAP)). A day ended by going to bed wakes at wakeHour.

waterFx._doc: Living water on the inner map (ui/innerMapLayers/waterFx.js): surf on sea/lake shores, gentler on ponds and river banks (from/to in tiles off the land edge, period in seconds; kinds = strength by water kind), sparkles on open water and ripples on ponds (assets/lpc/FX/Water Reflections.png), sparkles and streaks of foam running down the river along each cell's own flow (streaks), splashes where waves break (Splash.png). weather scales speed, reach, splash frequency and sparkle.

streaks._doc: The current: flecks of foam and darker ripple lines streaming down each river cell along its own flow (t._flow). density: share of river cells with one; speed: tiles a second mid-channel; travel: how far one slides (tiles, mid-channel; bankTravel by the banks); length: art pixels [min, max]; bankSlow: speed by the banks (share of mid-channel); eddy: how fast it curls over a ford.

deck._doc: Aboard at sea: the water lapping the hull (overrides surf).

wake._doc: Aboard and under way: the bow wave and the wake behind the stern (in tiles).

water._doc: Ponds, rivers, lakes and their shores on the inner map (world/innerMap/water.js). Ponds per terrain: subTerrains.*.waterFeatures { chance, count, radius (cells), lobes }, scaled up on a wet hex. rivers: radius (half-width in cells) and how it widens per river flowing in, how far its gates wander along the map edge, meander, the bends it swings in (bend: how far to either side, bendLength: cells per bend), what crossing a street (and running beside one, and the map border) costs the route, how far it keeps from buildings, fords in the wilds [min, max]. lake: the band of shore along the sides of a lake hex that face land. deep: how many cells from land water turns deep, by kind. dressing: chances per cell (reeds on shallows/bank, cattails and lilies on still water by the shore, stones on the bank, stepping stones on a ford) and the sprite cells ([col, row], 32px) of the LPC plants and rocks sheets.

palms._note: Palms in the wild (world/innerMap/palms.js): which palm props (data/townProps.json), on which ground, and per terrain the chance a cell grows one - oasis: within nearWater cells of water, chance: anywhere else. Not on a town's map.

_undergrowthNote: The chance a cell the wild trees left grows a bush (the tp_bush_* props, data/townProps.json; world/innerMap/terrain.js scatter).

treeDensity._note: Share of the usual wild trees a terrain's inner map grows (world/innerMap/terrain.js scatter; 1 = as on grassland).

cliffs._note: Raised crags in rocky country (world/innerMap/cliffs.js): how many on a hex, and their width, the depth of their top and the height of the rock face below in tiles, the chance a big one carries a second step up (tier), and the share with an angled front (5+ wide) rather than a square one. A settlement hex gets 40% of them.

wilds._comment: Wilderness encounters (player/wilds.js, world/innerMap/encounters.js): a wilderness hex holds encounters with tileChance, 1..maxPerMap of them from its biome list, placed by a hash of the world seed — never on the centre (minFromCentre) and minApart from each other.

rabbit.name: Wild Rabbit
rabbit.description: A small rabbit darts through the grass.
rabbit.text: A fat brown rabbit freezes at the edge of a warren, nose working. The grass here is cropped short and riddled with holes; there must be dozens of them under your boots.

choices.label: Set a snare at the warren mouth

success.text: By the time your pipe is smoked out, two rabbits hang kicking in your loops.

failure.text: The snare springs on nothing. The rabbits watch you from three holes away, entirely unbothered.

success.text: It jinks the wrong way into a bramble and you have it by the ears.

failure.text: You put your foot straight down a burrow and go sprawling.

choices.label: Sit still and watch the warren

success.text: The rabbits come out to feed around you. Where they graze, you find clover, sorrel and wild strawberries.

deer.name: Gentle Deer
deer.text: A hind stands in the long grass, ears turned to you like cupped hands. A fawn, all legs, wobbles behind her. Neither has decided to run yet.

success.text: One arrow, behind the shoulder. The fawn bolts. You have venison for a week.

failure.text: The shaft grazes her flank and both vanish into the grass, and your arrow with them.

success.text: They lead you down a game trail to a spring and a meadow you'd never have found, and from the rise above it you see a long way.

failure.text: A twig cracks. White tails flash and they are gone, leaving you somewhere you don't recognise.

success.text: You stand aside. The hind leads her fawn past you so close you could touch them.

herb_patch.name: Herb Patch
herb_patch.text: A sunny hollow is thick with yarrow, feverfew and something blue you half recognise. Bees work it lazily. Someone has been cutting here before you — the stems are cleanly trimmed.

success.text: You fill a cloth with the plants your grandmother would have named.

choices.label: Search for the rarer blue stuff

success.text: Bitter-blue, root and all — an herbalist would pay well for this.

failure.text: The blue flower turns out to be monkshood. Your fingers tingle and your stomach turns.

success.text: A hedge-witch from the nearest village arrives with her sickle, laughs at your patience, and tells you what the markets pay for herbs.

failure.text: Nobody comes. You lose the afternoon to bees and drowsiness.

traveler.name: Fellow Traveler
traveler.description: A weary traveler rests by the path.
traveler.text: A man in a dusty hood sits on a milestone, boots off, rubbing a blistered heel. A pack bigger than he is leans beside him. He nods at you warily, one hand never far from his staff.

choices.label: Share a meal and talk the road

success.text: He's a pedlar, it turns out, and over your bread he tells you exactly what pins, salt and wool fetch in the towns ahead.
He winces, then sighs. Grateful, he presses a few coins on you and swears to tell everyone of the kind stranger.
He drops the staff as soon as he sees your blade. His pack holds cloth, thread and a fat purse.

failure.text: The staff cracks across your skull before you've finished your threat. He limps off with everything he came with.

hidden_cache.name: Hidden Cache
hidden_cache.text: A flat stone at the foot of a lone oak has been moved and moved back — the grass beneath it is yellow. Scratched into the bark above, at head height, is a small arrow pointing down.

choices.label: Lift the stone
choices.hint: Certain, but someone may be watching

success.text: A greased leather bundle: a few coins, dried meat and a coil of good rope. Smugglers' rations, most likely.

choices.label: Read the marks before touching anything
choices.hint: Wits; it may be a waymark

success.text: The arrow is one of a chain. You follow the marks through three more trees to a second, richer cache — and a scrap of map.

failure.text: You puzzle over the marks until a needle trap in the bundle pricks your thumb. It swells, hot and ugly.

choices.label: Take a little, leave something in trade

success.text: You take only the rope and leave a candle. Honest dealing between strangers who will never meet.

wolf.name: Wolf Pack
wolf.text: Grey shapes keep pace with you between the trunks — four, maybe five. A lean she-wolf stops on a fallen log and watches you with unhurried yellow eyes. They are hungry, and they have not yet decided.

choices.label: Stand your ground and make yourself big
choices.hint: Nerve. A fire or a weapon helps

success.text: You roar, stamp and swing. The pack melts back into the trees and leaves you be.

failure.text: One darts in low and gets its teeth into your calf before the rest lose interest.

success.text: Two clean shots and the pack scatters, leaving you good grey pelts.

failure.text: Your arrow goes wide and the pack comes for you instead.

choices.label: Throw them your meat and back away

success.text: They fall on the meat snarling at each other. You are long gone before they look up.

fox.name: Cunning Fox
fox.description: A fox watches from the underbrush.
fox.text: A red fox sits in the bracken with something in its jaws — a small leather pouch, its drawstring trailing. It looks at you, looks at the pouch, and seems to grin.

success.text: It drops the pouch to leap a ditch. Inside: a silver ring and a few coins someone will be missing.

failure.text: You chase it through brambles and a bog. It sits on the far bank and watches you climb out.

success.text: Its earth is a magpie's nest of stolen things: buttons, a spoon, a purse, a wedding band.

failure.text: It loses you in a dozen loops through the bracken. You're fairly sure it was enjoying itself.

choices.label: Toss it a strip of meat

success.text: It drops the pouch, snatches the meat, and is gone. Fair trade. Inside are herbs and a few coins.

snake.name: Venomous Snake
snake.text: A thick adder lies across the path, sunning itself on the warm earth, its zigzag back almost invisible against the dry grass. It is between you and where you mean to go.

success.text: You give it a wide berth through the thistles and lose nothing but time and a little skin.

choices.label: Pin it with a forked stick and milk the venom
choices.hint: Steady hands. A hunter or herbalist knows how

success.text: You pin the head and coax the venom into a stoppered vial. Apothecaries pay well for this.

failure.text: It twists free and strikes your wrist. The arm swells to the elbow by nightfall.

success.text: One heavy stone and it is done. Its skin is fine and patterned.

failure.text: You miss. It doesn't.

bear.name: Brown Bear
bear.description: A massive bear forages for berries.
bear.text: Among the pines a great brown bear is stripping a bilberry bush with delicate, absurd care. It is the size of a hay cart. It has not seen you. The wind is in your favour — for now.

success.text: Step by careful step, you leave the bear to its breakfast. Further along you find the bushes it hasn't reached yet.

failure.text: A branch snaps underfoot. The bear rears, roars, and you run like you have never run. You keep your skin, mostly.

choices.label: Take the bear
choices.hint: Deadly. Combat, strength and a spear

success.text: It is a long, terrible minute. Then the bear is down and you are alive, and every hunter in the north will hear of it.

failure.text: One swipe throws you into a tree. You come to with the bear gone, a broken arm and a lesson.

choices.label: Leave it honey and slip past

success.text: You roll the honey-pot downwind. The bear's nose goes up, and it lumbers away after it, happy as a child.

elk.name: Bull Elk
elk.description: A majestic elk with impressive antlers.
elk.text: A bull elk stands knee-deep in snow among the pines, breath smoking, antlers spread wider than your arms. It bugles once, a strange high whistle, and the forest goes quiet to listen.

success.text: A long stalk through the snow, one true arrow. Meat to feed a village and a rack of antler to make a carver weep.

failure.text: It turns and charges. You throw yourself aside into a drift and lie there while it crashes off through the trees.

success.text: Where the bull scrapes his trees, last winter's antlers lie half-buried in the snow.

failure.text: Nothing but bark scrapings and cold fingers.

success.text: It stands a long time, then walks off with great dignity. You feel, oddly, that you have been granted an audience.

lion.name: Savanna Lion
lion.description: A lion rests in the tall grass.
lion.text: A maned lion lies on a termite mound, belly full, flicking flies with his tail. His pride sprawls in the shade below. He has seen you. He does not care — yet. Your path runs straight past them.

success.text: A long detour through the grass, and the pride never stirs.

failure.text: A lioness rises to look at you and you run, which is exactly the wrong thing. You escape, but not cleanly.

success.text: You walk past like a king passing beggars. The old lion yawns. The herdsmen who watched will tell of it.

failure.text: Your nerve breaks at the last. A lioness gives chase for sport and catches your leg.

success.text: Three arrows, a charge you will dream of, and a mane for your wall. The herdsmen hail you a hero.

failure.text: The pride comes for you all at once. You escape up a thorn tree, bloody and shaking.

elephant.name: Elephant Herd
elephant.text: A herd of elephants moves across the grass in a slow grey river, calves trotting between the legs of their mothers. The old matriarch's tusks are yellow and long, one broken at the tip. They are heading, unhurried, for water you cannot see.

success.text: They lead you to a hidden waterhole ringed with fruit trees. You drink and fill your packs.

failure.text: The matriarch decides you are too close and charges. You run, and do not stop for a mile.

success.text: They pass close enough to hear their bellies rumble. You feel small and glad of it.

choices.label: Look for where the old ones die
choices.hint: Intelligence. Ivory lies where elephants go to die

success.text: In a gully choked with grass, great bones lie bleaching — and tusks among them, long abandoned.

failure.text: You find only a dry gully and a sun that does not forgive.

parrot.name: Colorful Parrot
parrot.text: A scarlet-and-gold parrot lands on a vine above you and says, quite clearly, 'Pay the toll! Pay the toll!' in a sailor's voice. It has a scrap of brass ring on one leg. Somebody, once, owned this bird.

success.text: It hops onto your wrist and recites, between bites, half a sailor's song about a cove 'where the three palms lean'.

failure.text: It snatches the fruit, bites your thumb and flaps off cackling.

choices.label: Sit and listen to what it says
choices.hint: Intelligence. Birds repeat what they hear

success.text: Between curses it chants a merchant's price list — word for word, and recent.

failure.text: You learn many new and colourful oaths, and nothing else.

choices.label: Catch it to sell
choices.hint: Nimble hands. A fine bird fetches a price

success.text: You net it in your cloak. A merchant at the coast will pay for a talking bird — you sell it soon after.

failure.text: All you catch is a beakful of your own earlobe and a few bright feathers.

panther.name: Black Panther
panther.description: A panther stalks through the jungle.
panther.text: The birds stop all at once. On a branch above the path, a black cat as long as a man lies watching you with eyes like hammered gold. Its tail flicks once. Below it, half hidden in the leaves, is the carcass of a deer.

choices.label: Keep perfectly still and back away

success.text: Step by step you withdraw. The cat yawns, uninterested. Your heart takes an hour to slow.

failure.text: A twig snaps. It drops like black water and rakes your shoulder before vanishing.

success.text: You meet its leap with your blade. The pelt is the finest you have ever seen.

failure.text: It is faster than anything alive. You drive it off at the cost of a torn side.

choices.label: Steal the deer while it watches

success.text: You drag the carcass off and the cat merely watches, as if amused. Good meat tonight.

failure.text: It objects. Strongly.

scorpion.name: Giant Scorpion
scorpion.description: A large scorpion scuttles across the sand.
scorpion.text: A scorpion the length of your forearm, amber as old honey, sits in the shade of the only rock for a mile. It raises its tail as you approach. You are very hot, and that is the only shade.

choices.label: Pin it and cut off the sting
choices.hint: Quick hands. The venom is worth coin

success.text: One swift stroke. Apothecaries pay for the sting; the venom sac alone will do for poison.

failure.text: The sting finds your wrist. Your arm swells and burns, and the sun swims.

choices.label: Shoo it away with a stick

success.text: It sidles off, offended. You rest in the shade until the worst of the heat passes.

failure.text: It won't budge. You go on through the glare without rest.

success.text: You walk on under your hat. It costs you sweat but nothing worse.

mountain_goat.name: Mountain Goat
mountain_goat.text: A shaggy billy goat stands on a ledge no wider than your hand, chewing thoughtfully and staring at you. Below him a narrow trail winds along the cliff face — goat-made, goat-worn, and probably a shortcut if you are brave or foolish enough.

choices.label: Follow the goat track along the cliff
choices.hint: Strength and nerve. A rope helps

success.text: The track crests a shoulder of rock and the whole valley lies open below you, every road and river laid out like a map.

failure.text: A ledge crumbles under your boot. You catch yourself, but not before the rock takes skin and wind from you.

choices.label: Take the billy for meat
choices.hint: A hard shot on a steep slope

success.text: He drops where he stands and slides, mercifully, toward you rather than off the edge.

failure.text: Your arrow clatters off the rock. The goat looks at you with something like contempt and vanishes over the ridge.

choices.label: Watch where the herd goes to drink

success.text: The goats lead you to a seep of cold water and a scatter of shed hair caught on the thorns. You drink deep and pick a few hardy hill herbs.

eagle.name: Golden Eagle
eagle.text: A golden eagle wheels in the thin air above a crag, then drops into a cleft where a great untidy nest of sticks is wedged. Feathers drift down the cliff — and something glints among the twigs of the eyrie. Magpies are not the only birds that collect.

choices.label: Climb to the eyrie
choices.hint: Strength. Rope helps; the eagle will not like it

success.text: With the mother screaming overhead you snatch what glitters — a silver cloak-pin and a handful of old coins — and plenty of fine feathers besides.

failure.text: The eagle hits you like a thrown sack of knives. You slither back down, bleeding from the scalp.

success.text: Long golden flight-feathers lie in the scree — a fletcher's treasure.

choices.label: Read the eagle's flight as an omen

success.text: The bird rides the wind three times round the peak and away east. You feel, absurdly, that you have been given permission for something.

failure.text: It flies off without the courtesy of meaning anything. You feel faintly foolish.

giant_frog.name: Giant Frog
giant_frog.description: An enormous frog croaks from the murk.
giant_frog.text: Something the size of a hound squats on a drowned log, throat swelling and sagging like a bellows. Its croak shakes the reeds. Marsh folk say the skin of such a frog sweats a poison that kills rats and cures warts, depending on how much you use.

success.text: After a struggle that will keep the marsh birds laughing for weeks, you have the beast — and a marsh-wife pays well for its sweat.

failure.text: It kicks you into the black water. You come up spitting, and the water was not clean.

choices.label: Scrape its skin carefully for venom

success.text: Rubbing a dock-leaf poultice on your hands first, you scrape off a vial's worth of milky sweat.

failure.text: Your hands go numb to the wrist, then your lips. You sit in the reeds a long time waiting to see if you will die.

success.text: You leave it to its kingdom of mud and gather marsh plants while it croaks at your back.

polar_bear.name: Polar Bear
polar_bear.description: A polar bear surveys its icy domain.
polar_bear.text: A white bear the size of a hay-cart rises from behind a ridge of snow, nose working, black lips drawn back. It has been feeding on a seal; the snow round it is pink. It has seen you. It is deciding whether you are dessert.

success.text: It is a long and terrible minute. Then the great white thing lies still, and you are standing. The tale will travel before you.

failure.text: One swipe throws you across the ice like a doll. You crawl away while it returns to its seal.

success.text: Step by slow step you put a ridge between you. It goes back to its meal.

failure.text: It follows a little way, huffing, then charges — a short charge, a warning. It is enough to leave you bruised and shaking.

choices.label: Wait, and take what it leaves of the seal

success.text: Hours later it ambles off full. You get blubber, a good seal-hide, and frostbitten fingers.

reindeer.name: Reindeer Herd
reindeer.text: A river of grey-brown backs flows across the tundra, hundreds strong, steaming in the cold. Clicking hooves and grunts fill the air. Far off on a rise, a few figures in fur stand with long staffs — the herders, watching you as closely as the herd.

choices.label: Pick off a straggler
choices.hint: Hunting craft. The herders may object

success.text: A lame yearling falls behind; you take it cleanly. Meat and a thick winter hide.

failure.text: The herders' dogs come at you, and their masters' words are worse. You leave with nothing but bites.

success.text: They share hot fat-tea in their skin tent and tell you of the migration routes and the old cairns of their ancestors.

failure.text: They watch you approach, then simply move the herd on. You never get within shouting distance.

choices.label: Gather shed antlers along the trail

success.text: The herd's passing leaves a scatter of shed antlers in the moss — carvers prize them.

arctic_fox.name: Arctic Fox
arctic_fox.description: A white fox blends with the snow.
arctic_fox.text: A white fox, almost invisible against the snow, is digging furiously at a drift. It stops, ears swivelling, nose black against the white, and eyes the pack on your back. It has clearly done this to travellers before — and lived on it.

success.text: A loop of cord and a scrap of meat, and the finest white pelt you have ever held is yours.

failure.text: The fox takes the bait, slips the snare, and while you are fiddling with it steals your supper from your pack.

choices.label: See what it is digging for

success.text: It unearths a cache of lemmings — and beside it, half-buried, a traveller's lost pouch with a few coins and some salt.
It snatches the meat and trots ahead of you for a mile, as if to show you the way. It leads you round a crevasse hidden under snow.

sea_turtle.name: Sea Turtle
sea_turtle.description: A sea turtle rests on the beach.
sea_turtle.text: A great turtle has hauled herself up past the tideline, flippers working slowly at the sand. She is digging. Her eyes stream with salt, as if she were weeping. Gulls are already circling the spot.

choices.label: Guard her nest from the gulls

success.text: You keep the gulls off till she has covered her eggs and dragged herself back into the surf. A fisher who saw it all nods at you.

choices.label: Dig up some of the eggs

success.text: Leathery eggs, a dozen. Good eating, and you try not to look at her.

failure.text: She swipes at you with a flipper hard enough to knock you flat.

choices.label: Leave her, and comb the beach

success.text: Along the wrack line you gather what the tide has given.

horse_herd.name: Wild Horses
horse_herd.description: A herd of wild horses grazes freely.
horse_herd.text: A dozen shaggy horses graze the open plain, manes knotted with burrs. A dun stallion keeps himself between you and the mares. Among them is a young grey that would carry a rider well, if anyone could get close.

success.text: A long, sweating afternoon, and at last the grey stands blowing at the end of your rope, ears forward. It will follow you.

failure.text: The stallion comes at you screaming. You let go of the rope just in time to keep your ribs — almost.

success.text: The grey eats from your hand, then follows you a while across the grass. Riding alongside the herd, you see where the land opens out.

failure.text: The stallion snorts and the whole herd wheels away, leaving you with an empty sack.

success.text: Something in you lifts watching them go thundering off toward the horizon. You walk on lighter.

sheep.name: Mountain Sheep
sheep.description: Hardy sheep graze on the hillside.
sheep.text: A dozen half-wild sheep graze the hillside, their fleeces matted and long overdue for shearing. One ewe is caught fast in a bramble thicket, bleating piteously. There is no shepherd in sight, only an old stone fold with a fallen wall.

choices.label: Free the ewe from the brambles

success.text: She trots off without a word of thanks, as sheep do, leaving tufts of wool on the thorns for you.

failure.text: She kicks, the thorns bite, and you come out bloody-armed — though she is free.

choices.label: Take a sheep for the pot

success.text: Mutton tonight, and nobody the wiser.

failure.text: The sheep scatter in every direction, and a boy with a sling appears on the ridge, shouting. A stone catches you on the ear.

choices.label: Mend the fold wall and wait for the shepherd

success.text: At dusk a grizzled shepherd comes down, sees the wall, and shares cheese and the news from the market towns.

songbird.name: Forest Songbird
songbird.text: A small brown bird sings from a hazel bough, pouring out a song so long and liquid it seems impossible from such a little throat. The whole glade is gold with autumn leaves.

success.text: You don't know how long you sit. When you rise the weight on your shoulders has lifted.
You whistle it back, badly, then less badly. It will go down well in the taverns.

failure.text: The bird stops, offended, and flies off. You're left whistling to yourself.

choices.label: Look for its nest and the trees around

success.text: You leave the nest be, but the hazels around it are heavy with nuts and the brambles with blackberries.

failure.text: Wasps. A great many wasps.

spider_nest.name: Spider Nest
spider_nest.text: Sheets of web hang between the ferns, heavy with drops, thick as sailcloth further in. Something the size of a dog shifts in the gloom at the heart of them. Wrapped bundles hang there too — and one of them has a boot sticking out.

choices.label: Burn the webs
choices.hint: Needs a lantern or oil. Fire is certain

success.text: The silk goes up with a hiss. Among the ashes you find what the last traveller carried.

choices.label: Hack your way to the bundles
choices.hint: Combat. It will not like this

success.text: You drive the thing back into the dark and cut down a purse, a knife, and a dead man's charm.

failure.text: It drops on you from above. You tear free with a burning welt on your neck.

choices.label: Back away quietly
choices.hint: Nobody needs to be brave today

success.text: You give the webs a wide berth. Some silk stuck to your sleeve — a weaver might want it.

hermit.name: Forest Hermit
hermit.description: An old hermit lives among the pines.
hermit.text: A hut of turf and pine boughs leans against a boulder, a thread of smoke rising from it. An old man with a beard like lichen sits outside carving a spoon. He doesn't look up, but he says, 'Took you long enough.'

success.text: He talks of the old kings and the folk before them, and of a place to the north that isn't on any map. Most of it sounds mad. Some of it doesn't.

failure.text: He talks for hours, entirely about spoons.

success.text: He eats it slowly, with great respect. Then he presses on you a pouch of dried herbs: 'For the cough you'll get in a week.'

choices.label: Ask him to look at your wounds

success.text: He makes a poultice of moss and spruce resin and slaps it on without asking. It stings like fire and works like a miracle.

failure.text: His poultice smells like a dead badger and does about as much good.

herbalist.name: Wandering Herbalist
herbalist.text: A young woman with green-stained hands and a satchel of bundled roots is crouched over a patch of comfrey, muttering Latin-sounding names. She looks up hopefully: 'You wouldn't happen to have a knife sharper than this one?'

success.text: A salve for wounds and a pouch of good herbs, made with care.
She cleans and binds your hurts with brisk competence and refuses payment: 'Practice.'

failure.text: Her remedy is still experimental. It helps a little and makes you sneeze a great deal.

success.text: A long afternoon in the glades. She is a fine teacher; you come away with a satchel of your own and a better eye.

failure.text: You grab a fistful of nettles thinking them mint. She laughs until she has to sit down.

druid.name: Forest Druid
druid.description: A druid tends to the forest.
druid.text: An old woman in moss-green wool is splinting the broken limb of a young cedar with willow strips. Her hair is braided with feathers and she does not look up. 'If you've come to cut,' she says, 'keep walking.'

success.text: She works in silence, then tells you the old names of the hills hereabouts and what lies past them.

choices.label: Ask her to teach you the plants
choices.hint: Charisma. She is not easily charmed

success.text: By dusk you can tell heal-all from hemlock blindfolded. She sends you off with a pouch of her own.

failure.text: She hears the town in your voice and turns her back. The forest seems a little colder.

choices.label: Ask her to look at your hurts

success.text: She chews leaves into a poultice, slaps it on, and tells you to stop whining. It works.

prospector.name: Prospector
prospector.text: A wiry old prospector squats in a hill stream, swirling his pan with the patience of a heron. His mule regards you sourly. "Claim's mine," he says without looking up, "but I'll sell you a day's panning — or a tale, if you've ale."

success.text: By sunset the bottom of your pan glitters. Gold dust, and a nugget the size of a pea.

failure.text: Gravel, gravel and more gravel. The prospector grins at the coins in his palm.

choices.label: Share a drink and his tales

success.text: Two cups in he tells you where the old miners found their silver, and three cups in he draws you a map on a scrap of hide.

failure.text: He drinks your beer, tells a long story about a mule, and falls asleep.

choices.label: Ask what ore fetches in the towns

success.text: He knows every assayer and smelter in three valleys and their prices to the copper.

shepherd.name: Highland Shepherd
shepherd.text: An old shepherd sits on a boulder with a crook across her knees and two black-and-white dogs at her feet, watching her flock scatter over the slope. She has watched you coming for the last mile. 'You'll be lost, then,' she says.

success.text: She knows every path in these hills and the price of wool in every town that buys it, and tells you both.

failure.text: She answers in grunts. You learn that it will rain, which you knew.

choices.label: Help her bring a ewe down from the crag

success.text: You haul the bleating fool down by the scruff. She pays you in wool and the best cheese you've ever eaten.

failure.text: The ewe gets down by itself in the end. You do not, and come down the hard way.

success.text: She drives a fair bargain and throws in a story about her grandmother and a wolf.

fisherman.name: Old Fisherman
fisherman.text: An old man stands in the shallows with his trousers rolled, casting a line into the surf with a flick of his wrist. A basket at his feet holds three silver fish. He spits, and doesn't look round. 'Fish don't like talkers.'

success.text: You land two before he does and he respects you after that.

failure.text: You lose his hook to the weed. He says nothing at length.

success.text: After an hour he talks: of the coast, the coves, and the price of fish in the harbour towns this year.

choices.label: Trade him something for his catch

success.text: Bread for fish, a fair trade, and he throws in a tale of a wreck up the coast nobody has picked over.

woodcutter.name: Woodcutter
woodcutter.text: The steady thock of an axe leads you to a broad-shouldered man felling a beech. He has a dozen logs stacked, a mule to drag them and a temper visibly frayed by a jammed saw.

choices.label: Lend him your back for an hour

success.text: Together you free the saw and split the lot. He pays you in firewood and tells you the shortcuts through the forest that only woodmen know.

failure.text: A log rolls the wrong way and takes the skin off your shin.

success.text: Good seasoned planks, a fair price, and a grudging grin.
Woodmen hear everything. He tells you of an old place deep in the forest where his father wouldn't cut, and why.

failure.text: He grunts and goes back to his saw. You've caught him on a bad day.

forager.name: Mushroom Forager
forager.text: An old woman in a moss-coloured shawl prods the leaf litter with a hazel stick, a basket on her hip already heavy with caps and gills. She glances at you and pointedly covers the basket with a cloth.

choices.label: Ask her to teach you the good ones

success.text: She thaws, and walks you through the wood: this one for the pot, this one for the fever, that one never. You come away wiser and with a full cloth.

failure.text: She tells you the death-cap is 'a fine eating mushroom' and watches to see if you believe her. You don't — quite. Your stomach is unhappy anyway.

success.text: She counts the coin twice and hands over the lot, with a truffle tucked under the cloth as a parting kindness.

choices.label: Follow her to her secret patch

success.text: She leads you, all unknowing, to a ring of beeches thick with chanterelles.

failure.text: She turns, sees you behind a tree, and curses you in a dialect older than the kingdom. You have bad dreams for days.

nomad_camp.name: Nomad Camp
nomad_camp.description: Desert nomads have set up camp.
nomad_camp.text: Black goat-hair tents are pitched in the lee of a ridge, camels kneeling around them like boulders. A man with a falcon on his fist steps out to meet you, hand on his knife but courtesy in his voice. 'Guest or thief?' he asks.

success.text: Coffee, dates, and talk until the stars come out. They know every well and market for a hundred leagues.

failure.text: They give you water, as the law requires, and no more. You sleep outside the tents.

choices.label: Trade for spices
choices.hint: Commerce. They drive a hard bargain

success.text: After an hour of theatrical outrage on both sides, you come away well pleased.

failure.text: They had the better of you, and smiled while doing it.

choices.label: Sit with the elders and listen

success.text: The eldest tells of the tribes' first coming to the sand, and of a city the dunes swallowed.

tribal_camp.name: Tribal Camp
tribal_camp.text: Round huts of wattle and thorn stand inside a ring of stakes, cattle lowing in the kraal. Children run to stare at you; a warrior with an ochre-painted face steps out and plants his spear in the ground, waiting to hear what you want.

success.text: They feed you millet and sour milk, and the headman's mother tells of their ancestors' long walk south.

failure.text: Something you do offends. You are escorted politely but firmly beyond the stakes.

success.text: Good iron is rare here. They give you a fine hide and a carved tusk for it.

failure.text: They take the tools gladly and give you a single hide, smiling.

choices.label: Offer to help with a sick child
choices.hint: Needs a healer's skill or remedy

success.text: The fever breaks by morning. They name you friend and show you the paths only they know.

bandit_camp.name: Bandit Hideout
bandit_camp.text: Smoke rises from a hollow screened by gorse. You count four men around a fire, one asleep, one tending a spit, two dicing. Horses tethered. A strongbox sits in plain sight under a cloak, as if nobody here can imagine being robbed.

choices.label: Creep in and take the strongbox

success.text: You belly-crawl through the gorse, lift the box and are half a mile off before the dice game ends.

failure.text: The sleeper wasn't asleep. You get away, but with an arrow's worth of hole in you.

success.text: Two fall, two run. The strongbox and their stolen goods are yours, and the roads hereabouts a little safer.

failure.text: You are outnumbered and they know it. You fight your way clear, bleeding, with nothing.

choices.label: Walk in openly and buy their goodwill

success.text: They laugh, take your coin, share their fire, and over stolen wine tell you which roads the lords' patrols ride and what the merchants are carrying.

failure.text: They take your coin, then your boots' worth more, and send you off with a kick for luck.

bandit_lookout.name: Bandit Lookout
bandit_lookout.description: A bandit watchpost on the hill.
bandit_lookout.text: On a knoll above the road a crude platform of lashed poles overlooks the valley. One man sits up there with a horn and a crossbow, eating an apple, watching the road and not the hill behind him. A smoke signal pile stands ready beside him.

success.text: He never finishes the apple. His pouch holds the gang's take for the week, and the road below is safer tonight.

failure.text: A twig cracks. He blows the horn and looses a bolt before running — and it does not miss.

success.text: You go up the poles roaring and he goes down the other side screaming. The towns will hear of it.

failure.text: He gets the horn to his lips and the hillside fills with his friends. You barely get away.

choices.label: Watch the watcher and learn their routes

success.text: By evening you know which paths the gang uses, and which they avoid — and the valley's lie besides.

witch_hut.name: Witch's Hut
witch_hut.description: A crumbling hut with strange symbols.
witch_hut.text: A hut on stilts leans over the bog, its door painted with eyes and spirals. Bundles of drying herbs and small bones hang from the eaves and clack in the wind. Smoke rises from the chimney. On the step, a black cat washes itself and does not trouble to run.

choices.label: Knock and ask for a cure or a fortune

success.text: A woman with river-green eyes takes your coin, reads your palm, laughs, and sends you away with a stoppered bottle and advice you did not ask for.

failure.text: She looks at you a long time, says "No," and shuts the door. That night you dream of drowning.

choices.label: Wait until she leaves, then raid the hut

success.text: Among the jars and jaw-bones you find salves, rare roots and a purse of odd old coins.

failure.text: The cat yowls. Something in the rafters falls on you in a cloud of grey dust, and your skin burns for days.

success.text: You sign yourself and walk on with your eyes ahead. Nothing follows. You feel blessed.

failure.text: Your prayer stumbles. Behind you the cat watches the whole way across the bog.

hidden_shrine.name: Hidden Shrine
hidden_shrine.description: An ancient shrine in the woods.
hidden_shrine.text: Behind a curtain of ivy stands a little stone house no taller than your chest, roofed with moss. Inside, a weathered figure holds out cupped hands. Someone has put fresh flowers in them — not long ago.

success.text: A stillness settles over you that you did not know you were missing. You rise with a lighter heart and lighter aches.

failure.text: Nothing comes. Only the drip of water, and the feeling of being politely ignored.

success.text: The letters are an old script, half-familiar. They name a god of the old folk and the year this grove was hallowed.

failure.text: Moss and time have eaten the words. You trace the shapes until your eyes ache.

choices.label: Look under the idol for offerings

success.text: Coins, old and green, pressed into the earth by generations of the hopeful. You pocket them. The wood seems colder on your way out.

fairy_ring.name: Fairy Ring
fairy_ring.description: A circle of mushrooms radiates magic.
fairy_ring.text: Under the copper beeches the toadstools stand in a perfect ring, the grass inside greener than it has any right to be in autumn. The air within hums faintly, like a held breath. Old folk say you should never step inside — or never step out.

choices.label: Leave an offering at the edge
choices.hint: Faith. Honey or bread pleases them

success.text: The hum softens into something like laughter. You wake from a doze you do not remember starting, rested and oddly lucky.

failure.text: Nothing answers. You walk away with the uneasy feeling of being laughed at.

success.text: The world tilts and rights itself. In your hand is a ring of pale gold you did not pick up.

failure.text: You dance till dusk without meaning to, and dream of thin grinning faces for nights after.

success.text: You take the caps and leave the stalks. Good eating, and nobody seems to mind.

failure.text: The caps you pick are not the caps you thought. Your belly cramps for a day.

mushroom_circle.name: Mushroom Circle
mushroom_circle.text: In a clearing the toadstools grow in a ring so perfect it might have been drawn with a compass. The grass inside is darker, greener, and utterly silent — no birds, no insects. Your grandmother would have told you never to step in.

choices.label: Step inside the ring
choices.hint: Luck. Old tales say it is unwise

success.text: Time slips. When you step out, the light has moved but you feel rested to the bone, and your pockets clink with old coins you did not have before.

failure.text: You step out at dusk, chilled, hungry and missing a day of your life you cannot account for.

success.text: Fairy-ring champignons, perfectly edible, and lots of them.

failure.text: You pick the wrong sort. The night is long and full of colours.

choices.label: Leave an offering at the edge and pass on

success.text: You set the honey on a stone. Walking on, you find the path easy and the weather kind.

ancient_carving.name: Ancient Carving
ancient_carving.text: A boulder streaked with lichen bears spirals, antlered figures and rows of notches cut deep into the granite. Someone stood here long before the first king, chipping at it with a harder stone, for reasons of their own.

success.text: The notches are a count of winters, the spirals a hunt. The rock is a story, and you can read the end of it.

failure.text: Spirals and stick men. Whatever they meant, they mean nothing to you.

success.text: A careful charcoal rubbing. Scholars in the cities collect such things and pay for them.

choices.label: Climb the boulder and look around

success.text: From the top you see the lie of the land for miles — and other boulders, carved like this one, marching off in a line.

failure.text: The lichen is slick. You come down a good deal faster than you went up.

old_well.name: Old Well
old_well.description: An ancient well, still with water.
old_well.text: A ring of mossed stones stands in a clearing where a farmstead must once have been; only nettles mark the walls now. The rope is long rotted, but you can hear water far below, and coins wink in the dark where wishes were made.

success.text: Cold, sweet water that tastes of stone. You feel the road wash out of you.
Elbow-deep in black water you scoop up a fistful of old wishes, and an older coin among them.

failure.text: A stone gives way and you drop the last few feet into freezing water.

choices.label: Toss in a coin and make a wish

success.text: The splash comes back sounding like a yes. Your step is lighter for the rest of the day.

failure.text: You never hear it land. You tell yourself that is a good sign.

frozen_corpse.name: Frozen Corpse
frozen_corpse.description: A body frozen in the ice, with possessions.
frozen_corpse.text: Half-buried in a drift at the foot of a pine sits a man, perfectly preserved, frost in his eyelashes. He looks almost peaceful. His pack is still on his back and one hand is clenched round something.

choices.label: Search his pack
choices.hint: Certain. The dead don't need it

success.text: Frozen bread, a flint, a few coins and good boots — no use to him now.
A folded scrap of oilcloth: a map, crudely drawn, with an X and a note in a shaking hand.

failure.text: The fingers will not open. By the time you give up your own hands are white and numb.

success.text: You heap stones over him and say what words you know. In his coat you find a letter to a wife in a nearby town; you'll see it delivered.

rumour.victim: the body of a lost traveller

frozen_ruins.name: Frozen Ruins
frozen_ruins.description: Ruins emerge from the melting ice.
frozen_ruins.text: The edge of a retreating ice sheet has given up a doorway: carved lintel, iron-bound door half open, a hall beyond sheathed in glassy blue. Meltwater drips somewhere inside like a slow clock. Nobody has walked here in a thousand winters.

choices.label: Read the carvings on the lintel

success.text: The script is old but kin to one you know. It names a people who lived here when the ice was young.

failure.text: The frost has eaten too much of it. You make out a word that might be 'king', or 'hunger'.

choices.label: Squeeze inside and search the hall

success.text: Behind the ice-curtain lies a stone chest. Within: tarnished coins and a fragment of something that hums faintly in your hand.

failure.text: A shelf of ice lets go above you. You are out before it finishes falling, but soaked to the bone.

choices.label: Sketch the lay of the land around it

success.text: From the ruin's high step you see how the old road ran, and set the valleys round it on paper.

failure.text: Snow-glare blurs every ridge into the next. Your sketch is mostly white.

buried_treasure.name: Buried Treasure
buried_treasure.text: The wind has scoured a dune down to its bones, and from the sand pokes the corner of an iron-bound chest, the wood bleached white. Nearby a ring of stones marks an old camp — and a tall cairn that might be a grave.

success.text: An hour of digging and the lid gives: old coin, a silver cup, and the smell of a hundred years.

failure.text: You dig in the full sun and the sand keeps pouring back. The chest holds rotten cloth and a few coins.

success.text: Under the top stone, wrapped in oilcloth, is the burier's map — this was not his only cache.

failure.text: It really is a grave. You put the stones back, feeling watched.

choices.label: Leave it — it may be cursed

success.text: You mark the place in memory and walk on with a clear conscience.

sunken_chest.name: Sunken Chest
sunken_chest.description: A chest half-buried in the muck.
sunken_chest.text: The corner of an iron-bound chest juts out of the bog where a peat bank has slumped. Water has blackened the wood, but the lock still holds. The muck around it sucks and gurgles, and bubbles rise from somewhere deeper — this ground wants to keep what it has taken.

success.text: With a sucking roar the bog gives it up. Inside, wrapped in oilcloth: silver, a jeweled brooch and a merchant's ledger in a dead hand.

rumour.victim: a chest drowned in the bog

failure.text: The bank slides and takes you with it up to the chest. You claw free coughing black water; the chest sinks out of sight.

choices.label: Prise the lid where it lies

success.text: The lid gives. You can reach only the top layer, but it holds a purse of coins.

failure.text: The lid stays shut, and a hinge snaps back and opens your thumb.

choices.label: Mark the spot and leave it

success.text: You note the landmarks carefully. The bog will keep it — or someone else will find it. Either way your map of these marshes is better for the looking.

washed_up_chest.name: Washed-Up Chest
washed_up_chest.description: The sea brought this chest ashore.
washed_up_chest.text: A sea-chest lies on its side at the tideline, iron straps rusted orange, a brass plate with a merchant's mark. Weed trails from the lid. The lock has held through whatever sank it.

success.text: The lid yields. Wet cloth, a purse of coin, a bottle of good spirit, sealed.

failure.text: The lock holds and your bar slips. You split your knuckles on the iron.

success.text: Click. Inside, everything is dry: coin, the merchant's ledger of prices, a compass.

failure.text: You jam the lock past saving. You'll have to leave it.

choices.label: Read the mark and carry word to its owner

success.text: You note the merchant's mark and send word on. Honesty is cheap out here, but someone will remember it.

pirate_cache.name: Pirate Stash
pirate_cache.text: Cut into a palm trunk: a crude skull, and an arrow pointing down. Beneath it, sand that has been dug and filled again, not long ago. Fresh boot-prints lead from the water. Whoever buried this may be coming back.

success.text: An iron box: coin, a string of pearls, a bottle of rum. You are gone before the longboat rounds the point.

failure.text: The pirates come back while you're still waist deep. You run, but not before a cutlass finds you.

success.text: Two pirates come, argue over a chart, and leave it on the rock while they drink. You borrow it.

failure.text: They spot you in the palms. You run, and lose your purse on the way.

success.text: Wise. You hear oars an hour later, and laughter, and are glad you are elsewhere.

message_bottle.name: Message in a Bottle
message_bottle.description: A sealed bottle with a message.
message_bottle.text: A green glass bottle bobs in the shallows, corked and sealed with black wax. Through the glass you see rolled paper, and something small and heavy rattling at the bottom.

choices.label: Break the seal and read it

success.text: A castaway's plea, and a crude map of an island no chart you know shows. At the bottom, a single old coin.

failure.text: Seawater got in long ago. The ink is a blue cloud. The coin, at least, is gold.

success.text: Collectors pay for such things unopened. You wrap it carefully.

choices.label: Throw it back for someone else

success.text: It belongs to whoever the sea means it for. You throw it far and feel strangely good.

abandoned_cart.name: Abandoned Cart
abandoned_cart.description: A merchant's cart left on the road.
abandoned_cart.text: A two-wheeled cart lies on its side in the ditch, one wheel shattered. Crows have been at a sack of grain. There is no ox, no driver — only a muddy boot, and drag marks leading off toward the long grass.

success.text: Wet grain, a crate of cheap pottery and a forgotten purse under the seat.

choices.label: Follow the drag marks
choices.hint: Someone may be alive. Tracking and nerve

success.text: Not wolves — the carter himself, crawling with a broken leg. You splint it and get him to the road. His gratitude is loud and his purse generous.

failure.text: The trail ends at a trampled patch and a lot of blood. Whatever took him might still be near; you leave quickly.

success.text: Under the seat, a soggy tally-book: what he bought, where, and what he hoped to sell it for.

failure.text: The book has been rained into pulp. You can make out only the word 'salt', underlined three times.

lost_explorer.name: Lost Explorer
lost_explorer.text: A thin man in a sweat-black coat sits against a strangler fig, scribbling in a ledger by the last light. His boots have rotted, his compass needle spins, and he has been eating, he admits, mostly ants. 'The river,' he croaks. 'Which way is the river?'

choices.label: Lead him out to the river

success.text: You bring him to the water by dusk. Weeping, he copies you a page of his survey.

failure.text: You find the river, but only after a night of leeches and fever-sweats for you both.

choices.label: Share your food and point the way

success.text: He eats like a wolf and presses a battered map on you. 'I won't need it again — never again.'
Twenty gold and a direction for his notes on every town he passed — prices included.

failure.text: He takes your coin, then clutches the ledger to his chest and won't let go. You leave with a copied page of nonsense.

castaway.name: Castaway
castaway.text: A sun-blackened figure is waving a shirt on a stick from a rock, shouting hoarsely. Beard to the chest, ribs showing. When you get close, he weeps and talks at once — a ship, a storm, three months, maybe four.

success.text: He eats like a wolf, then tells you everything: where his ship went down, and what was in its hold.
You bring his fever down. He presses his last treasure on you — a gold ring he kept through it all.

failure.text: He is too far gone for you. You sit with him until the end, and catch his flux.

choices.label: Ask what he knows of these waters

success.text: Between ravings he describes every cove and reef he's watched for months.

failure.text: He only talks about his mother's pies. You leave him some water.

rare_herb.name: Rare Herb
rare_herb.text: Between two dripping cedars, in a cushion of moss, grows a single stand of silverleaf — the herb physicians in the cities sell by the pinch. Its roots wind deep among the stones, and the bank beneath it is slick with rain.

choices.label: Dig it out root and all
choices.hint: Patient work. A forager's craft or tools help

success.text: You ease the whole plant free without breaking a root. It will keep for weeks.

failure.text: The bank slides out from under you and the roots tear. You save a few leaves and a bruise.

choices.label: Snip the leaves and leave the root
choices.hint: Safe, and it will grow back

success.text: You take what the plant can spare. Some old instinct tells you that was right.

choices.label: Sketch it and note the soil

success.text: Your drawing is good and your notes better. You understand now where such things grow.

failure.text: The rain smears your ink into a green blot. You pocket a few leaves anyway.

rare_orchid.name: Rare Orchid
rare_orchid.text: High on the trunk of a dead palm, out of reach of the monkeys, blooms an orchid striped white and violet like a noblewoman's sleeve. The perfumers of the south would pay its weight in silver — if it arrives alive.

success.text: You come down with the orchid wrapped in wet moss, roots intact.

failure.text: The dead trunk cracks and you fall into a thorn bush. The orchid falls with you, crushed.

choices.label: Gather seed pods from the ground

success.text: You find fallen pods, plump and dry — a gardener's treasure.

failure.text: The pods are empty husks, but you find something edible nearby.

choices.label: Leave it be
choices.hint: Some things should stay where they grow

success.text: You watch a hummingbird visit it, and go on your way lighter for it.

ore_deposit.name: Rich Ore Deposit
ore_deposit.text: A fresh fall of rock has split open the hillside, and the broken face is streaked with rust-red and a dull green bloom that miners call the copper flower. Here and there something brighter winks. Nobody has staked this — yet.

choices.label: Work the vein with your tools

success.text: By evening your arms are dead and your sacks are heavy with good ore.

failure.text: The face shears off without warning. You leap clear — mostly.

choices.label: Pick the loose pieces from the scree

success.text: A morning of stooping and squinting fills a pouch.

choices.label: Map the seam and sell the knowledge

success.text: Your careful sketch of the seam and its bearings will fetch a fair price from any mining guild — and teaches you the lie of the land.

rumour.victim: a map to a rich vein of ore

failure.text: The more you measure, the less sense the rock makes. You give up with a headache.

glowing_moss.name: Glowing Moss
glowing_moss.description: Moss that glows with an eerie light.
glowing_moss.text: In a gully where the canopy closes overhead, the rocks are furred with moss that glows a soft sea-green. Your hands look drowned in it. Insects drift through the light like slow sparks, and the silence is total.

success.text: Sealed away from the air, it keeps its glow. Pressed with oils it would make a fine elixir.

failure.text: The moss goes dark the moment you lift it, and leaves your fingers itching for days.

choices.label: Follow the glow down the gully

success.text: The moss runs like a path to a cave mouth no map shows, and from its lip you see far across the valley.

failure.text: The glow fades into ordinary dark and you stumble back up, scraped and lost for an hour.

choices.label: Sit a while in the light

success.text: Something in the quiet settles you. You leave rested, with a strange half-remembered dream of old kings.

old_mine_shaft.name: Abandoned Mine
old_mine_shaft.description: A dark mine shaft leads underground.
old_mine_shaft.text: Rotten timbers frame a shaft that drops into blackness. A rusted winch still hangs over it, and a cold draught breathes up smelling of wet stone and old lamp-oil. Scratched on the lintel in miners' marks: DEEP SEAM — DO NOT. The rest has flaked away.

choices.label: Climb down into the old workings

success.text: At the bottom the miners left in a hurry: a cracked lamp, a pick, and a sack of good silver ore they never hauled up.

failure.text: A rung gives way. You fall the last stretch in the dark and lie winded in black water.

choices.label: Strip the winch and timbers for salvage

success.text: Iron fittings and a good length of chain. Worth hauling to a smith.
The echoes tell you the workings run far — and the old marks on the beams name the people who dug them, long before any kingdom here.

failure.text: The stone falls a long, long time. Then something far below knocks back. You decide you have heard enough.

hidden_spring.name: Hidden Spring
hidden_spring.text: Behind a fold of rock and bracken, water wells up clear as glass into a stone basin worn smooth by centuries. Watercress grows at its lip. Someone once set a little carved head over it, now nearly weathered away.

success.text: The water is so cold it hurts your teeth, and tastes of stone and summer. You feel new.
The spring feeds a whole little garden of green things.

failure.text: Mostly bracken. You pick a little cress.

choices.label: Fill a flask and ask the old head's blessing

success.text: The water in your flask stays cold all day, and catches light oddly. Holy, the villagers would say.

failure.text: It is just water, very nice water. You drink it.

ancient_statue.name: Ancient Statue
ancient_statue.description: A weathered statue of unknown origin.
ancient_statue.text: Ferns and roots have half swallowed a stone figure twice your height: a crowned woman holding a bowl, her face worn smooth by centuries of rain. An inscription runs around the plinth beneath the moss, and the bowl still holds a little water.

choices.label: Clear the moss and read the inscription
choices.hint: Intelligence. A scholar would know the script

success.text: She was a queen of the old forest-folk; the inscription names her line and the war that ended it.

failure.text: The script defeats you, though you are sure one word is 'water' and another 'grief'.

choices.label: Drink from the bowl
choices.hint: Faith. A blessing or a curse

success.text: The water is cold as winter and tastes of iron. Your aches loosen and your thoughts clear.

failure.text: Rainwater, stagnant and green. You spend the night regretting it.

choices.label: Pry the gems from her crown

success.text: Two dull red stones come loose. They polish up nicely.

failure.text: Your blade snaps, the stones stay put, and the queen's blank face seems to frown.

hidden_temple.name: Hidden Temple
hidden_temple.description: A temple hidden by the jungle.
hidden_temple.text: Roots as thick as a horse's body have split a stepped temple of green stone. Carved serpents coil around the doorway, and the dark inside breathes out cool air that smells of wet stone and old incense. Monkeys watch you from the lintel.

choices.label: Go inside with a light
choices.hint: Needs a lantern. Luck in the dark

success.text: In the inner shrine a jade figure sits on a heap of offerings long since gone to green.

failure.text: A floor stone tilts. You catch yourself on the lip of a pit full of old spikes, and not quite in time.

success.text: The monkeys go quiet. A warmth fills you, as if something old approves of your manners.

failure.text: The silence feels like a door closing in your face.

success.text: The serpents tell a story: a people who came from the sea and the god who drowned their enemies.

failure.text: The carvings are too worn to follow, though you sketch a few for someone wiser.

pict_stones.name: Pictish Stones
pict_stones.text: Three standing stones lean together on the hilltop, covered in carvings: a crescent and a broken rod, a beast with a long snout, a comb and mirror. Lichen fills the grooves. Someone has left a sprig of rowan at the foot of the tallest.

success.text: It is a lineage, told in pictures — who came over the hills, and who drove whom out.

failure.text: The beast with the long snout stares at you. You are no wiser.

choices.label: Leave an offering beside the rowan

success.text: The wind drops and the stones seem to settle. Walking away, you feel unaccountably lucky.

failure.text: Nothing happens. A crow takes your coin when you've gone ten paces.

success.text: Lined up, the three stones point to a notch in the far hills — and something on the other side the old folk thought worth marking.

failure.text: They point at a bog. You are fairly sure of that.

frozen_artifact.name: Frozen Artifact
frozen_artifact.text: Locked a hand's depth inside a block of old ice is a worked thing of gold and dark stone — a clasp, perhaps, or the head of a sceptre. The ice around it is cloudy, as if it breathed once.

success.text: Flake by flake it comes free, whole and heavier than it looks.

failure.text: A crack runs through the block and the thing inside breaks with it. You salvage a few gold fittings.

choices.label: Melt it out with a fire

success.text: Slow heat does what force would not. It slides into your hand, and something about it makes you think of a dead king's name.
The ice splits clean and the artifact tumbles out unharmed.

failure.text: Ice shards fly. One opens your cheek; the artifact lies in pieces.

ice_crystals.name: Ice Crystals
ice_crystals.text: In a wind-scoured hollow, frost has grown into towers and fans of crystal taller than a man, clear as glass and humming faintly when the wind blows across them. Locked in the ice at the heart of one is a dark shape — a stone, or a box, or something that was alive once.

choices.label: Chip out what is frozen inside

success.text: Inside is a fist-sized lump of rose-quartz threaded with true gems, as if the ice had grown round a treasure.

failure.text: A crystal fan shatters and the shards fly. One opens your cheek to the bone.

choices.label: Sit and listen to the humming

success.text: The notes rise and fall like a chant you almost know. You come away feeling clean and light, and strangely rested.

failure.text: You sit too long. When you stand, your feet are white and wooden.

success.text: You fill a page. Scholars in the south will not believe it, but the hollow makes a fine landmark for your maps.

aurora_spot.name: Aurora Viewpoint
aurora_spot.description: The best view of the northern lights.
aurora_spot.text: A bare rise above the tundra, ringed with knee-high standing stones. As the dark comes down, the sky catches fire — green curtains, rippling, with crimson at their hems. The stones are worn smooth on their tops, as if many people have sat here over many centuries to watch exactly this.

choices.label: Keep vigil through the night
choices.hint: Faith; it will be bitterly cold

success.text: Somewhere before dawn the lights seem to bend down toward you. You do not know what was said, but you understood it.

failure.text: The lights are glorious and the cold is merciless. You stagger off at dawn feverish and shaking.

choices.label: Take bearings from the stars between the lights

success.text: Between the curtains the stars are sharp as nails. You fix your position better than any chart could, and see far across the plain by the green light.

failure.text: The lights wash out the stars and your figures come out nonsense.

success.text: Faint marks on the stones record a people who counted the lights by the generation.

ice_spirit.name: Ice Spirit
ice_spirit.description: A spectral presence in the ice.
ice_spirit.text: A face looks up at you from inside the clear ice — not frozen there, but moving, mouthing words you cannot hear. Frost spreads in fern-patterns from where your shadow falls. The air tastes of iron and old snow.

choices.label: Pray for its rest
choices.hint: Faith. Holy water or a priest helps

success.text: The face closes its eyes. The frost-ferns melt to water, and something in the ice lets go with a sigh you feel in your teeth.

failure.text: It hears you, and it does not like what it hears. Cold slides under your skin and stays there.

choices.label: Lay your ear to the ice and listen
choices.hint: Risky. It may have something to say

success.text: Through the ice comes a whisper of a place it knew in life — a sheltered valley no map remembers.

failure.text: The voice is only cold, endless cold. You come to yourself shaking, your cheek stuck to the ice.

choices.label: Back away without turning your back

success.text: You step back, and back, until the face is just a smudge in the ice. Then you walk quickly.

ice_elemental.name: Ice Elemental
ice_elemental.description: A being made of living ice.
ice_elemental.text: What you took for a pressure ridge unfolds itself: a hunched thing of blue ice twice your height, grinding as it moves. Snow whirls around it in a slow ring. It has not seen you yet, or it does not care.

success.text: Your blow finds a seam and it bursts into a storm of shards. At its heart lies a stone of frozen blue fire.

failure.text: Its fist of ice clips you and the world spins white.

success.text: You slip by in its snow-shadow. Behind where it stood, the ice has given up an old frozen pack.

failure.text: Snow crunches. It turns, and the cold that rolls off it bites through your furs as you run.

choices.label: Hide and wait for it to pass

success.text: It grinds away into the white after an hour. You are stiff and frozen, but whole.

blizzard_zone.name: Blizzard Zone
blizzard_zone.text: The wind comes off the ice sheet without pause, carrying snow sideways in a hissing wall. You cannot see your own hand held out. Somewhere in the white, a rhythmic clank — metal on metal, like a bell or a loose shutter.

success.text: You come out the far side half-frozen but proud, and the land lies spread clear beneath you.

failure.text: You walk in a circle for an hour and come out where you started, shaking.

success.text: A trapper's hut, a loose iron latch. Inside: a stocked shelf and a trapper long gone south.

failure.text: The sound stops. You have no idea which way you came.

choices.label: Dig in and wait it out

success.text: In a snow hollow you wait until the wind drops at dusk. Cold, cramped, alive.

ice_bridge.name: Natural Ice Bridge
ice_bridge.text: A span of blue ice arches over a crevasse that goes down further than the light does. It is wide enough for one, ribbed with old wind-scour. On the far side, a ledge — and on the ledge, something dark that might be a pack.

success.text: Step by step. On the ledge: a dead climber's pack with coin and a good lantern.

failure.text: Your foot skids and you hit the ice hard, sliding to the very edge before you stop.

choices.label: Chart the crevasse field from here

success.text: From the bridgehead the cracks make a pattern you can draw, and a safe path through.

failure.text: The glare defeats you. You note only 'here be cracks'.

success.text: You turn back. The crevasse sighs cold air at your back as you go.

will_o_wisp.name: Will-o'-the-Wisp
will_o_wisp.description: Mysterious lights dance in the mist.
will_o_wisp.text: Pale blue lights bob over the marsh in the dusk mist — three, then five, then one. They drift away as you watch, then pause, as if waiting for you. The marsh folk say they lead fools to drowning and the wise to treasure, and that nobody knows which they are until it is over.

success.text: They lead you to a sunken causeway of ancient stones, and at its end a little hoard of offerings — coins and an old carved amulet.

failure.text: The lights go out all at once. You are waist-deep in black water with no idea which way is land, and you are out all night.

success.text: You notice they rise where the marsh gas bubbles. A natural thing, then — but where they gather, bog-iron lies thick.

failure.text: The longer you watch the more they seem to look back. You sleep badly.

success.text: You walk away. Something behind you sighs, or it is only the wind in the sedges.

leech_swarm.name: Leech Swarm
leech_swarm.description: The water is infested with leeches.
leech_swarm.text: The only way across is a black channel, waist-deep and still. When you put a stick in, a dozen fat leeches fasten to it within the count of ten. Barber-surgeons in the towns buy leeches by the jar — but they will want yours alive, and not full of you.

success.text: You come out the far side, pull them off with salt and swearing, and press on.

failure.text: Halfway across you go into a hole. By the time you crawl out the leeches have drunk deep and the bites are already swelling.

choices.label: Trap leeches in a jar to sell
choices.hint: Cunning; a healer knows the trade

success.text: A bit of raw meat on a string, a stoppered pot — and a barber-surgeon's supply for a season.

failure.text: They get into your sleeves faster than into the jar.

success.text: A long detour through the sedges brings you round dry-shod, and past a stand of useful marsh plants.

mirage.name: Desert Mirage
mirage.description: A shimmering mirage on the horizon.
mirage.text: Out where the heat dances, a lake glitters among palms and white towers. Your tongue is thick in your mouth. You know what a mirage is. You also know that sometimes, out here, there really is water.

choices.label: Head for the water
choices.hint: Luck. Could be death, could be life

success.text: Behind the shimmer is a real seep: brackish, but water. From the dune above it you see a long way.

failure.text: The lake recedes and recedes. You turn back at last, cracked-lipped and reeling.

choices.label: Read the land instead
choices.hint: Intelligence. Where would water truly be?

success.text: Dark scrub in a dry wash, and birds circling low — you dig and find damp sand, then water.

failure.text: You dig a hole in hot sand and find only more hot sand.

choices.label: Wait out the heat under your cloak

success.text: You sleep through the worst of the day. The mirage is gone by evening; so is your thirst's sharpest edge.

sand_wurm.name: Sand Wurm Sign
sand_wurm.description: Something large moves beneath the sand.
sand_wurm.text: The dune ahead ripples like a horse's flank, and a long low ridge creeps across the flat toward the rocks. Bleached ribs stick up from the sand nearby — a camel, or what is left of one. The ground trembles faintly under your boots.

success.text: You reach the stone as the sand erupts behind you. Something huge and eyeless sinks back down, disappointed.

failure.text: The ground bucks and throws you. You crawl onto the rocks bruised and half-buried.

success.text: It passes beneath you like a ship's keel and is gone. In its wake the sand has turned up old bones and a bronze clasp.

failure.text: It notices. The sand opens and you are flung out by a heave of muscle, scraped raw.

choices.label: Follow it at a distance
choices.hint: Hunter's craft. Where does it lair?

success.text: It surfaces at a hidden pan of salt and old caravan wreckage — easy pickings, and a tale for the taverns.

failure.text: You lose its track in the heat and lose your bearings with it.

cave_bats.name: Colony of Bats
cave_bats.description: Bats swarm from a cave entrance.
cave_bats.text: At dusk a black ribbon pours out of a crack in the mountainside — thousands of bats, squeaking at the edge of hearing. The ground before the cave is deep in guano, and the reek is astonishing. Farmers in the lowlands pay for that muck. Somewhere inside, water drips.

choices.label: Go in while they are out hunting
choices.hint: A lantern helps a great deal

success.text: Behind the bat-roost the cave runs deep, and in a dry pocket someone long ago hid a strongbox. Its lock has rusted to nothing.

failure.text: The colony comes home early. In the shrieking dark you blunder into rock, and something bites.

choices.label: Shovel guano to sell to farmers

success.text: You fill sacks with the stuff, gagging. The farmers of the valley will pay for it — eventually, once you have bathed.

choices.label: Watch the flight and move on

success.text: The bats stream out against a violet sky for nearly an hour. It is, you admit, rather beautiful.

rockslide.name: Recent Rockslide
rockslide.description: A rockslide blocks part of the path.
rockslide.text: The path ends in a raw tumble of boulders, dust still settling. A mule's leg sticks out from under one stone, and from somewhere under the heap you hear a faint, steady knocking — someone is alive in there.

choices.label: Dig them out
choices.hint: Strength; tools or a strong companion help

success.text: Hours of heaving bring out a dusty, weeping tinker, alive. He presses his purse on you and swears to tell every tavern between here and the coast.

rumour.victim: a tinker buried in a rockslide

failure.text: A second slide comes down as you work. You drag him out at last, but the stones have had their share of you.

success.text: The packs hold good tools and a bolt of cloth. The knocking goes on behind you for a long while.
You pick your way round, and from a nearby village send men back with shovels. That will have to do.

failure.text: Loose stone slides under you and you go down hard.

hermit_sage.name: Mountain Sage
hermit_sage.description: A wise hermit lives near the summit.
hermit_sage.text: Near the summit, in a hut of piled stone roofed with turf, an old man sits wrapped in goat-hair blankets, perfectly still, snow in his beard. He opens one eye. "You climbed a long way," he says. "Either you want something, or you are lost. Usually both."

choices.label: Ask him what he has learned up here

success.text: He talks until the stars come out — of kings before kings, of who first named these peaks. You come down with your head ringing.

failure.text: His riddles leave you feeling like a child at a lecture. He seems to enjoy that.

choices.label: Leave him food and ask nothing

success.text: He eats slowly, nods once, and at the door tells you of a place below the snowline that no map shows.

choices.label: Ask him the safe paths down

success.text: He draws the passes in the frost on his doorstep with a crooked finger.

lost_expedition.name: Lost Expedition
lost_expedition.text: A collapsed tent, a sled with one runner snapped, and three shapes under the snow you decide not to look at closely. A leather satchel is lashed to the sled. The last entry in a frost-stiff journal is dated two winters ago.

success.text: Rope, lamp oil and a wrapped bundle of dried meat, still good in this cold. They will not need it.
Between the complaints about the cold are careful bearings — they were close to something when the storm took them.

failure.text: The ink has run with meltwater. You can read only a name, over and over, and the word 'sorry'.

success.text: You raise a cairn over them and say what words you know. Under the last body lies a purse they were saving for home.

rumour.victim: the bones of a lost expedition

failure.text: The ground is iron. You manage a poor cairn and leave with cracked hands and a cough.

baobab_tree.name: Ancient Baobab
baobab_tree.text: The baobab is wider than a farmhouse, its bark grey and wrinkled like an elephant's hide, its branches like roots clawing at the sky. Generations of travellers have cut marks into its trunk, and a hollow at its base is big enough to stand in.

success.text: Under a flat stone in the hollow, someone left a cache wrapped in oiled leather.

failure.text: A colony of bats explodes out of the dark into your face.

success.text: The cuts are a code — water two days east, a camp to the north. The country opens out in your mind.

failure.text: Mostly names and the occasional obscene drawing.

success.text: The fat gourds are full of tart, chalky pulp. You eat, rest in the shade, and fill your bag.

vultures.name: Circling Vultures
vultures.text: A spiral of vultures turns over a dip in the grass a few hundred paces off, and more drop down to join it. Something is dead there, or dying. In the heat-haze you think you see a cart's wheel jutting up.

choices.label: Go and see
choices.hint: Could be a beast still feeding

success.text: A merchant's cart, overturned, the oxen dead and the driver long gone. His strongbox survived.

failure.text: Hyenas are already at the carcass. They do not share.

success.text: Under the cart a boy is still breathing. You get him to the nearest herdsmen; his father is a trader and pays you in news.

failure.text: You come too late. You bury the dead as best you can and carry their sorrow away with you.

choices.label: Leave the dead to the birds

success.text: You keep walking. The birds keep circling.

highland_cow.name: Highland Cattle
highland_cow.text: A dozen shaggy red cattle stand knee-deep in heather, fringes over their eyes, horns wide as a man's arms. A bull lowers his head at you, more curious than angry. A brand on the nearest cow says someone owns them.

choices.label: Drive a stray back to its owner

success.text: The crofter is grateful, gives you cheese, and tells you what cattle and wool fetch at market this season.

failure.text: The cow decides it does not want to go anywhere, and kicks you to make the point.

success.text: A heavy, brutal job. You leave with more meat and hide than you can easily carry.

failure.text: The bull takes exception. You are lucky to escape over a dyke with only bruises.

success.text: The bull snorts and goes back to his heather. A shepherd's trail runs past them, and you take it.

coconut_crab.name: Coconut Crab
coconut_crab.description: Large crabs climb the palm trees.
coconut_crab.text: A crab the size of a dog is halfway up a palm trunk, claws clamped into the bark, dropping coconuts with a dull thump. Its claws could take a finger off. It has noticed you.

success.text: Wrapped in your cloak and trussed, it is the best eating on the island.

failure.text: It gets a claw on your hand and does not let go for a very long time.

success.text: It has done the climbing for you. You gather the fallen nuts and anything else edible under the palms.
It drags a coconut to a crevice full of shiny rubbish — buttons, a ring, a brass buckle.

failure.text: It disappears into a hole in the rocks. That's the end of that.

hermit_crab.name: Hermit Crab
hermit_crab.text: Dozens of hermit crabs are trundling across the sand in a line, swapping shells in a strange queue, each sizing up the next. One has crammed itself into something that is not a shell at all — it glints.

success.text: It is a gold thimble, or a little cup. The crab is most offended. You give it a whelk shell for its trouble.

failure.text: It nips your finger to the bone and vanishes into a hole.

success.text: A bucketful of small crabs and a few shellfish from the rocks.

choices.label: Watch the shell-swap to its end

success.text: It is the most orderly thing you have seen since you left town. You laugh out loud, and feel lighter for it.

tropical_fruit.name: Tropical Fruit
