tropical_fruit.text: A grove of fruit trees hangs heavy over a stream: yellow fingers, red-skinned globes, something spiked and green that smells like a sweetshop. Monkeys chatter in the canopy, and a few fruits lie bitten on the ground.

success.text: You eat until juice runs down your chin and pack the rest.
Custard-sweet and heavenly. You save the seeds — some merchant will pay for these.

failure.text: It is not ripe, or not meant for people. Your belly lets you know for a day.

choices.label: Climb for the best at the top

success.text: From the treetop you can see the whole coast, and the best fruit besides.

failure.text: A monkey defends its fruit with real conviction. You come down faster than you went up.

snow_rabbit.name: Snow Rabbit
snow_rabbit.description: A white rabbit hops through the snow.
snow_rabbit.text: A white rabbit sits up in the drift, only its black eyes and the pink of its ears giving it away. Its tracks run in neat pairs toward a thicket of buried juniper. The cold has made it fat and slow.

choices.label: Set a snare along its run

success.text: By the time your fingers ache the snare has done its work. Fat meat and a soft white pelt.

failure.text: The rabbit sniffs your snare, considers it, and hops around it. You stamp your numb feet and give up.

choices.label: Follow its tracks to the juniper

success.text: Under the snow-heavy juniper the ground is bare, and you scrape up frozen berries and a handful of hardy herbs.

choices.label: Watch it a while and let it be

success.text: It washes its face with both paws, unbothered by the whole frozen world. You feel oddly warmer for having seen it.

shipwreck.name: Old Shipwreck
shipwreck.description: The hull of an old ship rests here.
shipwreck.text: A ship lies on her side above the tideline, ribs showing through rotten planking like the bones of a whale. Her figurehead — a crowned woman — stares up at the sky. The stern cabin is still closed, and the tide is coming in.

success.text: The captain's cabin: a strongbox, the log, and a sextant green with age.

failure.text: The tide catches you inside. You get out through a hole in the hull, gashed and half-drowned.

success.text: Good seasoned oak and a coil of tarred rope that still holds.
Water-stained but legible: her last voyage, her ports, and the prices she paid for her cargo.

failure.text: You find it, but it falls to pulp in your hands.

hawk.name: Red-tailed Hawk
hawk.description: A hawk hunts over the hillside, a jess trailing from one leg.
hawk.text: A red-tailed hawk drops on a vole not twenty paces away, mantles over it, and glares at you. A leather jess and a little silver bell still dangle from its leg — someone's lost hunting bird, gone half wild. Falconers pay dearly for a trained hawk, and lords more dearly still.

choices.label: Lure it to your fist with meat
choices.hint: Patience; costs meat. A hunter knows how

success.text: After an hour of stillness it steps onto your glove. The bell is stamped with a lord's crest — the steward of his house pays a handsome reward for its return.

failure.text: It snatches the meat, rakes your wrist for good measure, and is gone.

success.text: The hawk quarters the hillside, and following it you learn the hollows where game lies up.

choices.label: Shoot it for the bell and feathers
choices.hint: Needs a bow. A cruel end

success.text: It falls. The silver bell is real silver; the feathers are fine. It feels like less than it should.

failure.text: The arrow hisses past and the hawk is away over the ridge, bell tinkling mockingly.

frozen_traveler.name: Frozen Traveler
frozen_traveler.description: A traveller huddles in the snow, near death from cold.
frozen_traveler.text: A shape in the snow that you took for a stone turns out to be a man, curled round a dead fire, rime on his eyebrows and lips gone blue. His eyes flicker when you shake him. "Couldn't... get it lit," he whispers. His pack bulges, and his boots are better than yours.

choices.label: Build a fire and warm him back to life

success.text: By midnight he is shivering, which is a good sign, and by dawn he can talk. He is a fur-factor, and he tells you what pelts are fetching in the towns, and swears your name will be blessed in them.

rumour.victim: a fur-factor freezing in the snow

failure.text: He dies a little after midnight, holding your hand. You sat out in the cold all night for it.

choices.label: Carry him toward the nearest shelter

success.text: You stagger into a herders' camp at dusk with him on your back. They take him in, and take you for a hero.

rumour.victim: a traveller half-frozen in the snow

failure.text: Halfway there the wind rises. You make it — he does not — and the cold has got into your chest.

choices.label: Take his boots and pack — he's past saving

success.text: Good boots, furs, a little purse. He watches you go. You tell yourself he was past saving.

shrine_wayside_offering.name: Wayside Offering Stone
shrine_wayside_offering.description: A weathered shrine heaped with travellers' offerings.
shrine_wayside_offering.text: A squat stone shrine leans by the track, its saint worn faceless by rain. Around its foot lie copper coins, dried flowers, a child's carved horse and a twist of incense still faintly smoking. Whoever passed last did so this morning.

success.text: You add your coins to the pile and kneel. The ache in your shoulders eases, and the road ahead seems shorter.
You rest your forehead on the cool stone. It asks nothing, and gives a little peace.
You scoop up the coppers and walk on whistling. The saint has no face to frown with.

failure.text: A shepherd boy on the hill sees you do it and runs to tell the whole valley.

shrine_weeping_saint.name: The Weeping Saint
shrine_weeping_saint.description: An old temple where a statue is said to weep.
shrine_weeping_saint.text: In the gloom of a roofless temple stands a marble saint with streaks down her cheeks. A thin bead of water gathers at one eye as you watch, and falls. Pilgrims have scratched their prayers into every inch of the plinth.

choices.label: Catch the tears in a flask
choices.hint: Faith; a priest knows the rite

success.text: The drops come steadily into your flask, clear and cold. It feels heavier than water should.

failure.text: You wait until dusk and catch a few drops of what is, you suspect, only rain through a crack.

success.text: Beneath the newer pleas you find an older script telling who first raised this place, and why.

failure.text: The scratches blur into a thousand lost sons and failed harvests. Your eyes ache.

success.text: You pray with your palms on her cold feet. Something in your chest loosens.

shrine_pilgrim.name: Footsore Pilgrim
shrine_pilgrim.description: A pilgrim rests at the shrine, too lame to go on.
shrine_pilgrim.text: An old pilgrim sits against the shrine wall with his boots off and his feet wrapped in bloody rags. He is three weeks from home and two from the holy city, he says, and he will not make either on these feet.

choices.label: Dress his feet
choices.hint: Healing salve or herbs; a healer helps

success.text: Clean, salved and bound, his feet will carry him on. He blesses you and tells you of a strange place he passed on the road.

failure.text: You do what you can, but the wounds are angry. He thanks you anyway and limps away slowly.

success.text: Over the bread he tells you the old stories of this shrine and the price of salt in every town he passed.

choices.label: Give him your horse... or your purse

success.text: With your coin he can hire a cart to the holy city. He weeps and swears you will be in his prayers there.

shrine_desecrated.name: Desecrated Shrine
shrine_desecrated.description: Someone has smashed and fouled this shrine.
shrine_desecrated.text: The shrine has been broken open. Its saint lies in pieces in the nettles, its offering bowl is fouled, and a crude horned sign has been daubed in something dark across the lintel. The ash of a fire is barely cold.

success.text: You scrub the lintel, gather the pieces and reset the stones. By evening the place looks cared for again.

choices.label: Follow the desecrators' trail
choices.hint: Stealth; a hunter or spymaster helps

success.text: You find their camp at dusk and their stolen relics in a sack by the fire, and get away with them unseen.

failure.text: They were waiting. You get away, but not before a cudgel finds your skull.

success.text: The daubed sign blisters and fades as the water touches it. A weight lifts from the clearing.

failure.text: The sign will not wash out. That night your sleep is full of horns.

shrine_oracle_bones.name: Oracle Bones
shrine_oracle_bones.description: A bowl of carved bones sits on an ancient altar.
shrine_oracle_bones.text: On the altar of a moss-grown temple sits a stone bowl of knucklebones, each carved with a tiny rune. The pilgrims' custom, scratched on the wall, is plain: cast them, and read what they show. Nobody has written what happens if you read wrong.

success.text: The bones fall in a clear pattern — a road, a mountain, a door. You know, somehow, which way to go.

failure.text: The bones fall in a heap pointing at you. You feel watched all the way back to the road.

choices.label: Study the runes instead
choices.hint: Intelligence; a scholar or priest helps

success.text: The runes are a calendar of the old faith. In the margins someone recorded who built this place.

failure.text: The runes keep their secret. You copy a few for someone wiser.

success.text: You light a candle by the bowl and leave the bones uncast. Some doors are best left shut.

oasis_caravan_rest.name: Caravan Rest
oasis_caravan_rest.description: A trading caravan waters its camels at the oasis.
oasis_caravan_rest.text: Thirty camels kneel in the shade of the palms while their drivers brew bitter tea over dung fires. The caravan master, a heavy man with rings on every finger, eyes you over his cup. Traders talk, if you give them reason.

success.text: Over three cups of tea you learn what the caravan paid, and what it hopes to be paid, in the towns behind and ahead.
You drive a hard bargain and come away with spices worth twice what you paid.

failure.text: He smiles, takes your gold, and hands you a sack that turns out to be half sand.

choices.label: Offer to scout the next stage

success.text: You ride ahead and find the safe wells. The master pays well and you chart the dunes as you go.

failure.text: You lose the trail in a sandstorm and come back parched and empty-handed.

oasis_bitter_spring.name: Bitter Spring
oasis_bitter_spring.text: The pool at the heart of the oasis is clear and inviting, but the palms around it are yellowing and a dead jackal lies at the far edge. The water smells faintly of iron and something sweeter. Your waterskin is almost empty.

success.text: Bitter, but clean enough. You drink until your belly sloshes and fill your skins.

failure.text: By nightfall your guts are churning. The jackal knew something.

choices.label: Find what fouls it
choices.hint: Intelligence; an herbalist or healer helps

success.text: A seam of salt and copper-green leaks into the inflow. You dig a channel round it, and below, the water runs sweet. Under the seam lies raw ore.

failure.text: You dig in the heat for hours and find nothing but sand and a headache.

choices.label: Boil a little and drink sparingly

success.text: Boiled and cooled, a few cups keep you going. It is not pleasant, but it is safe.

oasis_date_grove.name: Date Grove
oasis_date_grove.description: Heavy clusters of dates hang from the palms.
oasis_date_grove.text: The oasis is ringed with date palms bowed under their fruit. Half the crop lies fermenting on the sand, humming with wasps; the best hangs high, gold and sticky in the crowns. Somebody planted these rows once, long ago.

success.text: You pick through the fallen fruit for the sound ones and eat your fill in the shade.
From the crown you cut down clusters fit for a prince's table — and spot ruins half-buried in the dunes beyond.

failure.text: The trunk is slick with sap. You come down a lot faster than you went up.

choices.label: Sleep the heat away in the shade

success.text: You sleep through the worst of the sun and wake rested, with dates for the road.

oasis_water_thief.name: The Water Thief
oasis_water_thief.description: Someone is fouling the oasis pool.
oasis_water_thief.text: A gaunt man in a ragged robe is tipping a bucket of carrion into the pool. Seeing you, he drops it and stands his ground, shaking. Fouled water drives the caravans to his brother's well a day east, he says, and his children are starving.

choices.label: Help him and clean the pool
choices.hint: Certain; costs a day's toil and some coin

success.text: You fish out the carrion together and give him coin for his children. He swears off the trick and tells you where the caravans are headed.
He flees east and does not look back. You clear the pool; the next caravan through rewards you for it.

failure.text: Desperation makes him vicious. He slashes you with a hooked knife before he runs.

choices.label: Make him an offer he can live with

success.text: You talk him into selling water from the oasis instead of fouling it. He pays you a cut in advance from his brother's hidden purse.

failure.text: He listens, nods, and the next morning the pool is fouled again. You drink from it before you notice.

monument_inscription.name: Graven Inscription
monument_inscription.description: A monolith covered in ancient script.
monument_inscription.text: A pillar of black stone stands alone on the rise, three times your height, every face carved with close, angular script. Lichen has eaten the lower lines; the upper ones are crisp as the day they were cut. Bird droppings crown it like snow.

choices.label: Puzzle out the script
choices.hint: Intelligence; a scholar or a rare book helps

success.text: Slowly the words give way: a king's boast, a war, a people driven into the sea. History no living tongue remembers.

failure.text: You recognise a word here and there — 'king', 'fire', 'never' — and nothing else.

choices.label: Take a rubbing to sell to a scholar

success.text: Charcoal over parchment, and the stone's words are yours to sell. Collectors pay for such things.
From the top you can see for leagues, and on the summit someone cut a crude map of the land.

failure.text: You slip on the droppings and fall badly.

monument_kings_cairn.name: King's Cairn
monument_kings_cairn.description: A great burial cairn of a forgotten king.
monument_kings_cairn.text: A mound of grey stones higher than a house, ringed with standing slabs. A carved crown marks the entrance stone. Grass grows over it, but a fox has dug a hole in one side, and through it you glimpse a gleam of metal.

success.text: You straighten a fallen slab and say the old words for the dead. The wind drops, briefly, as if in thanks.

choices.label: Widen the fox's hole and reach in

success.text: Your fingers close on gold: rings, a cup, old coins with a crowned head. Something in the dark seems to sigh.

failure.text: The stones shift and the hole collapses on your arm. That night the old king walks your dreams.

choices.label: Study the carvings on the slabs
choices.hint: Intelligence; a scholar or priest helps

success.text: The slabs tell of a king who united the hill tribes and of the kingdom that rose after him.

failure.text: Weathered spirals and broken figures; their meaning is gone with their makers.

monument_star_stone.name: Star Stone
monument_star_stone.description: A tower of stone aligned to the stars.
monument_star_stone.text: A lonely tower of fitted stone, roofless, its walls pierced by narrow slots at strange angles. On the floor a great disc is carved with lines and dots — the stars, you realise, and the hills, and roads that are no longer there.

success.text: Your copy is good. The old roads lead to places on no modern map.

failure.text: You copy it badly, but even a poor copy shows the lie of the land.

choices.label: Wait for night and watch through the slots

success.text: At midnight a single star burns in the slot over the eastern door, and the disc's lines suddenly make sense: one points to something hidden.

failure.text: Cloud rolls in. You spend a cold night on stone and see nothing.

choices.label: Shelter in the tower and rest

success.text: The old walls keep off the wind. You sleep well under the circling stars.

monument_toppled_colossus.name: Toppled Colossus
monument_toppled_colossus.description: A fallen giant statue lies broken in the grass.
monument_toppled_colossus.text: A stone giant lies face-down in the grass, its head the size of a cottage and its outflung hand still gripping a bronze spear gone green with age. Local folk have quarried its feet for walls. Its bronze crown, half-sunk in the turf, has not been touched.

success.text: You prise loose plates of the old bronze, heavy and worth a fair price at any smithy.

failure.text: The crown shifts and pins your hand against the stone.

choices.label: Rally the villagers to raise its head

success.text: With ropes, oxen and half the village you heave the great head upright to face the sunrise. They will sing of it in the alehouse for years.

rumour.victim: the giant's face raised to the sun

failure.text: The ropes snap and the villagers drift home grumbling about fools from away.

success.text: Under the hand you find votive coins dropped by long-dead worshippers, and a chip of the old gilding.

wreck_hold.name: Wreck's Hold
wreck_hold.description: A merchantman lies broken on the rocks.
wreck_hold.text: A merchant cog lies on her side among the rocks, her back broken, her hold half full of seawater. Crates bob in the flooded dark below the hatch. Gulls have had the crew. The tide is coming in.

choices.label: Climb down into the hold
choices.hint: Strength; rope and a lantern help

success.text: Waist-deep in black water you lash crates to your rope and haul them up one by one: cloth, wine, a strongbox.

failure.text: The tide surges in through the broken hull and slams you into a beam. You crawl out with nothing but bruises and a chill.

success.text: Along the tideline you find rope, a cask of salt fish and some splintered timber worth carrying.

choices.label: Find the captain's log
choices.hint: Intelligence; a scholar or merchant helps

success.text: Wrapped in oilcloth in the captain's cabin, the log lists her cargo, her ports and what she paid for every bale.

failure.text: The log is a sodden pulp. You can make out only a ship's name: the Patient Wife.

wreck_survivor.name: Wreck Survivor
wreck_survivor.description: Someone still clings to life on the wreck.
wreck_survivor.text: A thin cry carries over the surf. Out on the broken bowsprit of a wreck, a girl of perhaps fourteen clings with both arms, soaked and blue-lipped. The water between is a churn of rocks and foam.

success.text: You fight through the surf, get her on your back and bring her in alive. Her father is a shipwright in the nearest port, and he will not forget.

failure.text: The surf throws you against the rocks twice before you drag her ashore. She lives; you are not sure how you do.

choices.label: Throw her a line and talk her in

success.text: Your steady voice keeps her moving hand over hand along the line until you pull her out of the foam.

failure.text: She panics and lets go. You haul her out by the hair, half drowned, and spend the night warming her.

choices.label: Run for help from the village

success.text: The fisherfolk row out and bring her in. They thank you for the warning, if not for the courage.

wreck_drowned_bell.name: The Drowned Bell
wreck_drowned_bell.description: A bell tolls from a wreck beneath the waves.
wreck_drowned_bell.text: At low tide the masts of a sunken ship show above the water, and from somewhere below a bell tolls slow and muffled with each swell. Fishermen will not land here. On the shingle lies a sea-chest, its lid carved with a drowned saint.

success.text: Inside, wrapped in sealskin, lies a chart in a dead captain's hand marking a spot with a careful cross.

failure.text: The chest holds only a drowned man's clothes, and that night the bell tolls in your dreams.

choices.label: Row out and silence the bell

success.text: You cut the bell-rope and say the words for the drowned. The tolling stops; the fishermen will come back now.

failure.text: Something cold grips the oar. You row back hard with your heart hammering, the bell still tolling.

choices.label: Leave the dead to the sea

success.text: You walk away along the shingle. Behind you the bell tolls on, patient as the tide.
